name: Butterfly Guard Off-Balance
keyCorrections: If the sweep fails, your hook lost connection or you didn't off-balance enough — reset the hook and try again.
If they flatten your hook, you're too flat on your back — sit up on your far shoulder.
If they posture out of the collar tie, switch to an underhook or sleeve grip.
description: Use butterfly hooks, collar tie or underhook, and head positioning to break the opponent's base and create sweep, entry, or attack opportunities.
shortInstruction: Hook a leg, break posture, off-balance forward or sideways, then sweep or enter leg entanglements.
summary: Butterfly guard off-balance is the engine of the entire butterfly system. Without breaking the opponent's base, you cannot sweep or attack. The goal is to make them post a hand or step — then you move.
whyItWorks: Butterfly hooks create a lever on the opponent's center of mass — pulling them forward or lifting them sideways destroys their base.
The collar tie or underhook controls their upper body so your hook can work in isolation.
Off-balancing forces reaction: they either post (giving you an entry) or fall (giving you the sweep).
Danaher principle: you cannot sweep a well-based opponent. First break the base, then attack.
commonMistakes: Pulling on the collar tie without engaging the hook — the sweep comes from the hook, not the arms.
Letting your hooks get flattened or stripped before you off-balance.
Off-balancing sideways without controlling the far arm, allowing them to post and recover.
Staying flat on your back instead of sitting up on your shoulders to maintain hook pressure.
coachingCues: Hook first, then pull — the hook creates the off-balance, the arms guide it.
Sit up to activate the hook — flat hook is a dead hook.
Two-way threat: forward or sideways — they can't defend both.
safetySummary: Keep your head up and chin off your chest to protect your neck during collar ties.
Do not overcommit forward on a failed off-balance — you may expose your back to a front headlock.
Protect your ribs when the opponent drives forward hard — frame before they smash.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Win the hand fight → establish collar tie or underhook → insert butterfly hook → off-balance → opponent posts → sweep or enter leg entanglement.

decisionTree.action: go sideways. If they resist sideways, go forward. The dilemma is the system.
Off-balance options: forward (elevator sweep), sideways (pendulum sweep), or backward (arm drag to back take).

moneyDetails: Your butterfly hook should be deep — ankle behind their armpit area — not shallow on the thigh.
The collar tie pulls their head down to your chest level; this loads their weight onto the hook.
When they post a hand, attack that side immediately — that arm is now out of commission.
If they step back to avoid the sweep, extend the hook and transition to single-leg X or X-guard.
nextStep: After off-balancing, transition to butterfly sweep, single-leg X, or X-guard depending on their reaction.
fixItFast: Hook getting flattened? Sit up on your far elbow immediately.
They posture out? Switch to double sleeve grip and kick your hooks in deeper.
They step back? Extend the hook and enter single-leg X.
